newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian UES, Gazprom say low prices to hurt supply.
newsitem.headline: Russian UES, Gazprom say low prices to hurt supply.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and national power grid operator Unified Energy System (UES) said on Thursday that any cuts in the prices they charge would lower gas and electricity supplies.

President Boris Yeltsin told parliament on Thursday that natural monopolies' prices were unjustifiably high and fuelling a non-payments crisis, and he singled out the gas, electricity and rail transport sectors.
"A sharp fall in prices will lead to difficulties in gas deliveries," Gazprom spokesman Anatoly Kotov told Reuters.

He said Gazprom would have to cut gas production and reduce its investment programmes. As result, he said, the state would receive lower tax payments and dividends as a shareholder of 40 percent of Gazprom's shares.
"What shall we buy fuel with?" said UES spokesman Alexander Tarankov, adding that lower prices would mean less money for raw materials to fuel power stations.
He said a cut in electricity prices without a corresponding drop in prices for heavy fuel oil could make the power cuts in Russia's Far East a nationwide phenomenon.

The Primorsk regional administration in the Far East has prohibited power stations from raising tariffs, which the stations say has prevented them from buying natural gas and heavy fuel oil to run on.
Russia has already capped the prices Gazprom and UES can charge to industrial and residential customers.
The International Monetary Fund has urged Russia to restructure its natural monopolies by separating production and sales units and making costs more equitable and justified for certain sectors.
UES's Tarankov opposed such a restructuring, saying that if power producers became independent, they would raise prices for the regions to which they export supplies.
